youtube.title: Why Medicine Bottles Have a Foil Seal (7 Died in 1982)
youtube.description: Why do medicine bottles have a foil seal you must tear before you can take a single pill? Most people think it only keeps the medicine fresh. The real reason is darker. In 1982 seven people near Chicago died after taking Tylenol capsules that someone had poisoned after they left the factory. The case was never solved, but it changed packaging for every medicine you buy today. #TheHiddenWhy #facts #explained

sources: Chicago Tribune and Chicago Sun-Times coverage, Sept-Oct 1982
U.S. FDA history of tamper-resistant packaging regulations (1982-83) and the Federal Anti-Tampering Act of 1983
Harvard Business School and Time magazine case studies on Johnson & Johnson's 1982 recall
